statement_record.book: A strict monoidal category ⟨B,□,e⟩ is a category B with a bifunctor □:B×B→B that is strictly associative ((a□b)□c=a□(b□c) on objects and arrows) and an object e that is a strict two-sided unit (e□c=c=c□e, 1_e□f=f=f□1_e); bifunctoriality forces the interchange law and 1_a□1_b=1_{a□b}.
statement_record.intree: StrictMonoidal C = a @Monoidal C together with object-level Leibniz equalities ((X⨂Y)⨂Z=X⨂(Y⨂Z), I⨂X=X, X⨂I=X) and the requirement that tensor_assoc/unit_left/unit_right ARE the transported identities. The interchange law is automatic from tensor : C ∏ C ⟶ C being a Functor.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same — a faithful setoid encoding. The library builds StrictMonoidal on top of the relaxed Monoidal and then forces α,λ,ρ = id along on-the-nose object equalities, which is exactly Mac Lane's strict monoidal category (the extra α,λ,ρ=id data it carries is redundant, standard). Interchange is discharged by bifunctoriality, as Mac Lane notes.
